S18.01.note: The title is inferred from the first user message in apps/cli/src/sessions.rs (infer_title); the code the audit cited in tui_app.rs was not found. Whether the title is visible before the first save was not traced.
steps: Start agi and send a first message that has a clear topic, for example: Plan a birthday dinner for six people.
Send one or two more messages in the same conversation.
Type /sessions and press Enter.
Look at the row for this conversation: it should show a title made from your first message (cut at 50 characters, with ... if longer), with no naming step from you.
S18.01.where: agi, then type /sessions (or /history). Each row shows the date, the message count and a title taken from the first message.

S18.02.note: The picker's r key sends the side action complete:rename <id>; I did not trace how the prompt is filled, so the tester should check the exact prompt text on screen.
steps: Type /sessions and press Enter.
Move to a conversation with the arrow keys and press r.
Check what the prompt now shows (the code hands off a rename command with the session id filled in) and type the new title, then press Enter.
Type /sessions again and check that the row shows the new title.
Quit with agi and start it again, then type /sessions: the new title should still be there.
S18.02.where: agi, then type /sessions, select a row and press r (the hint reads r rename), or type /rename <id> <new title>.

S18.04.needs: a test conversation with a session id
S18.04.note: Archive and restore are terminal commands only; no archive control in the chat screen was found.
steps: Run agi session list and copy the session id of a test conversation.
Run agi session archive <session_id>; read the line Archived '<session_id>'. and the Unarchive with: hint.
Run agi session list: the conversation should be missing. Run agi session list --archived: it should be there.
Run agi session unarchive <session_id>; read Unarchived '<session_id>'.
Run agi session list again: the conversation should be back in the active list.
S18.04.where: Terminal, outside the chat: agi session archive <session_id>, then agi session unarchive <session_id>. List with agi session list, and agi session list --archived.

S18.05.note: The code deletes the session file; I did not verify that it also disappears from the chat picker or from cloud history, and the key used to answer the prompt was not traced.
steps: Pick a test conversation and run agi session show <session_id> to read its transcript.
Run agi session delete <session_id>.
Read the prompt Permanently delete session '<session_id>'? This cannot be undone. Answer no first; read Aborted. Session '<session_id>' was not deleted.
Run the delete again and confirm; read Deleted '<session_id>'.
Run agi session list and agi session show <session_id>: the conversation should no longer appear.
S18.05.where: Terminal, outside the chat: agi session delete <session_id> (add --force or --yes to skip the prompt).

S18.06.note: No command named duplicate exists; /fork creates a second session file, titled (fork) plus the original title (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs). Whether the new conversation is fully independent was not traced beyond the file write.
steps: Have a conversation with at least two exchanges.
Type /fork and press Enter and read the system message it shows.
Type /sessions: a new row titled (fork) followed by the original title should appear.
Open the new conversation and send a new message; then open the original and check it has no new message.
S18.06.where: agi, then type /fork (alias /branch) in a conversation with a few messages.

S18.09.note: The mode cycle changes the whole chat session; the code does not show it as a per-conversation setting separate from the session.
steps: Start agi and read the Mode: label; it should read Default.
Press Shift+Tab and read the new mode label (Plan, then Auto, then Bypass, then FullAuto, cycling).
Set Plan, send a request that asks for a file change, and check that it is treated as a plan rather than an edit.
Send a second request in the same conversation and check that it follows the mode you set.
Compare the mode you set with the Mode: label each time.
S18.09.where: agi, then press Shift+Tab in the chat; the Mode: label is shown above the input. Plan mode is also /plan.

S18.10.needs: a Local conversation; a signed-in account for Managed
S18.10.note: Switching an established session is refused with a message to start a new session; the flow is an explicit handoff rather than a plain switch.
steps: Type /privacy-settings and read the Privacy settings screen and the current mode.
Type /privacy-mode managed in a Local conversation.
Read Privacy mode was not changed. and the line that says Local -> Managed Cloud requires an explicit reviewable handoff.
Read the hint to run /continue-with-cloud and check that it describes the preview and consent step before anything is sent.
S18.10.where: agi, then type /privacy-settings to read the mode, and /privacy-mode local, byok or managed to switch (also /trust-boundary).

S18.15.needs: a conversation long enough to scroll
S18.15.note: A Mac keyboard has no End key; the tester may need the terminal's own key mapping for Ctrl-End. This was not verified against a terminal.
steps: Send a request that produces a long answer.
Scroll up with PageUp until the start of the answer is visible.
Press Ctrl-End (or End when the input is empty).
Check that the view returns to the newest message at the bottom.
S18.15.where: agi, then in the chat press Ctrl-End (also listed as Jump to the latest output in the keyboard help).

labels.text: already exists, so nothing was written

S18.18.note: Formats are Markdown, JSON and answer (last answer only); no PDF export was found. Relative file names are written under the workspace root.
steps: Have a conversation with several messages.
Type /export conversation.md and press Enter.
Read the message Exported the conversation to <path>. and open the file to check that it holds the whole conversation.
Type the same /export command again and read the message that says the file already exists and nothing was written.
S18.18.where: agi, then type /export, followed by a file name, for example /export conversation.md, /export json conversation.json or /export answer answer.md.

S18.21.note: Partial: /status does not show created time, id or project; the id is only in the sessions picker prefix and agi session show. Expected lists more fields than any one screen shows.
steps: Have a conversation with several messages.
Type /status and press Enter.
Read the Model, Mode, Turns and Tokens lines.
Type /sessions and read the row for this conversation: date and message count are shown.

S18.22.note: The report shows the token budget and sizes; I did not confirm that it names source files, instructions or memory individually. /memory is a separate command.
steps: Have a conversation with several turns and a file or two in context.
Type /context and press Enter.
Read the Context: bar with its percentage and token count, then the In context: breakdown.
Compare the breakdown with the expected items (files, instructions, memory, token budget).

labels.text: Session estimate (priced locally, not the billed figure)

S18.23.note: The figure is a local estimate labelled as not billed; the code totals come from the current session.
steps: Have a conversation with several turns.
Type /usage and press Enter.
Read Input tokens, Output tokens and the cache lines.
Read the Session estimate line and compare it with the conversation so far.

S18.24.note: No conversation-only instructions control was found. The cited apps/cli/src/lib.rs:237 is the --system-prompt startup flag for a whole run. Searched instruction in tui_app.rs, claude_parity.rs, repl/slash_commands.rs and repl/registry.rs; /output-style <name> --session is a style, not instructions.

S18.25.note: Only the startup flag --allowedTools (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:390) and /tools (list, a tool name, log, retry in apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs) were found. No per-conversation enable or disable control was found.

S18.27.note: I did not confirm that /tasks filters to tasks started from this conversation; it may list all tasks.
steps: Type /thread followed by a short task, for example: /thread summarise the README in this folder.
Type /tasks and press Enter.
Read the list of tasks and their status for the task you started.
Wait for it to finish, type /tasks again and compare the status with the Expected.
S18.27.where: agi, then type /thread with a short task, then /tasks (alias /task).

S18.28.needs: a signed-in account, a Managed privacy conversation, and a second device or browser
S18.28.note: The command is refused for Local and BYOK conversations (code gates on Managed privacy mode); the cross-device sync itself was not traced.
steps: Sign in with agi login and use a conversation in Managed privacy mode.
Type /continue-elsewhere and read the link and the words Continue it on the web.
Type /continue-elsewhere open to open it in the browser, or open the web or desktop app chat list on another device.
Find the same conversation there and send a message; check that it appears in this conversation.
S18.28.where: agi, then type /continue-elsewhere (add open to open it in the browser).
